desc: Derive and prove the reduction: building i visible from (0,h) iff slope (H_i-h)/X_i strictly exceeds max previous slope; answer = max over i of tangent intercept h*_i, with -1 if max < 0 (or N==1).

Implement upper convex hull of points (X_j,H_j) supporting: (a) tangent query — binary search for vertex maximizing intercept of line through (X_i,H_i) and hull vertex; (b) insertion of new point maintaining upper hull (pop while turn makes middle point non-maximal for intercept purposes). Use exact integer arithmetic (Fractions or cross-multiplication with Python ints) to avoid precision issues.

Handle the tangent query carefully: the intercept as a function of hull vertex index is unimodal; binary search comparing intercept(i, v) vs intercept(i, v+1) using exact comparisons: compare (H_v*X_i - H_i*X_v)/(X_i - X_v) vs (H_{v+1}*X_i - H_i*X_{v+1})/(X_i - X_{v+1}) via cross products (denominators positive since X_i > X_v).

Maintain hull insertion correctness: when adding point p_new with largest x, pop from the end while the new edge makes the previous vertex non-convex for an upper hull maximizing intercept (i.e., while intercept of line through hull[-2]..p_new is >= ... derive correct orientation: keep hull such that consecutive edge intercepts are strictly decreasing? Verify with examples).
Compute answer as max over candidates as a Fraction; if max < 0 print -1, else print with sufficient precision (e.g., format float or exact decimal via integer division with 20 digits).

Test against provided samples and edge cases (N=1, collinear points, decreasing heights, large coordinates) plus brute-force verification on small random inputs against an O(N^2) pair-max-with-validity checker.
